title: Malvaren (WHO PQ): clean SmPC
about: A prequalified paediatric antimalarial: the WHOPAR Part 4 SmPC with weight-band dosing, the MedDRA frequency table, the supplier, the WHO reference number and the dates.

fixed.intro: This summary of product characteristics focuses on uses of the medicine covered by WHO's Prequalification Team - Medicines. The medicine may be authorised for additional or different uses by national medicines regulatory authorities.

blocks.text: Malvaren 20 mg/120 mg dispersible tablets*
*Trade names are not prequalified by WHO. This is the national medicines regulatory authority’s responsibility.
Each dispersible tablet contains 20 mg arterolin and 120 mg lumexantine.
Excipient with known effect: each tablet contains 1.5 mg saccharin sodium. For the full list of excipients, see section 6.1.
Dispersible tablet. Yellow, round, flat tablets with a break line on one side and "SM" on the other. The break line is not intended for dividing the dose.
Malvaren is indicated for the treatment of acute uncomplicated malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum in infants and children weighing 5 kg to less than 35 kg.
Consideration should be given to official guidance on the appropriate use of antimalarial agents.

Disperse the tablets in a small amount of water (about 10 mL per tablet) and give the whole mixture at once. Give with food or milk to improve absorption of lumexantine. If the child vomits within 1 hour, repeat the dose.

items: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.
Known prolongation of the QTc interval or a family history of congenital QT prolongation.

subs.title: Special warnings and precautions for use

blocks.text: Malvaren is not indicated for severe malaria or for the prevention of malaria.
Lumexantine can prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution with other medicines that prolong the QTc interval and in patients with electrolyte disturbances.
If the patient does not eat, monitor closely, as exposure to lumexantine may be lower.

subs.title: Interaction with other medicinal products and other forms of interaction

blocks.text: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase lumexantine exposure; strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine) reduce exposure to both components and may cause treatment failure. Avoid medicines that prolong the QTc interval.

Pregnancy: data from more than 1000 exposed pregnancies in the second and third trimesters show no malformative or feto/neonatal toxicity. In the first trimester, use only if the expected benefit outweighs the risk, following national guidelines.
Breastfeeding: small amounts pass into human milk; breastfeeding may continue.

subs.title: Effects on ability to drive and use machines

blocks.text: Not relevant for the intended population.
Frequencies: very common (≥1/10), common (≥1/100 to <1/10), uncommon (≥1/1,000 to <1/100).
There is no experience of overdose. Give symptomatic and supportive treatment and monitor the ECG and serum potassium.

Pharmacotherapeutic group: antimalarials, combinations (fictional ATC). Arterolin, an artemisinin-type endoperoxide (fictional), rapidly reduces parasite biomass; lumexantine, a long-acting blood schizonticide (fictional), clears the remaining parasites.
Arterolin is absorbed rapidly (Tmax about 2 hours) and eliminated with a half-life of about 1 hour. Lumexantine absorption increases with food; its half-life is 3 to 5 days.
Embryo-lethality was seen with arterolin in rats in early pregnancy. Lumexantine was not genotoxic.
Microcrystalline cellulose, crospovidone, saccharin sodium, cherry flavour, colloidal anhydrous silica, magnesium stearate.
Not applicable.
24 months.
Do not store above 30°C. Store in the original package in order to protect from moisture.
Aluminium/aluminium blisters of 6, 12 and 18 tablets, in cartons.

subs.title: Special precautions for disposal and other handling

blocks.text: No special requirements.
